data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: reasonably
sections.summary: To a fair and acceptable degree; in a way that is sensible and not extreme.

senses.definition: to a fair and acceptable degree; in a way that is sensible, not extreme, and within normal limits
examples: The journey was reasonably short given the distance.

answers.answer: The apartment is reasonably priced.
The apartment is reasonable priced.
The apartment reasonably is priced.
The apartment is reasonably price.

sections.question: relatively
sections.summary: Compared to something else or to a general standard; to a certain degree.

senses.definition: to a certain degree when compared to something else or to a general standard; in a way that is measured against other things
examples: The new software is relatively simple to install.

answers.answer: This topic is relatively easy to understand.
This topic is relative easy to understand.
This topic relatively is easy to understand.
This topic is relatively easy for understand.

sections.question: scarcely
sections.summary: Almost not at all; only just; by a very small amount.

senses.definition: almost not at all; only just; used to say that something is nearly not the case or nearly does not happen
examples: He was so tired that he could scarcely keep his eyes open.

answers.answer: There was scarcely any time to prepare.
There was scarce any time to prepare.
There scarcely was any time to prepare.
There was scarcely any time for to prepare.

sections.question: sincerely
sections.summary: In a genuine and heartfelt way; honestly and without pretending.

senses.definition: in a genuine and heartfelt way; honestly and without pretending; used to express that feelings or intentions are real
examples: He sincerely hoped that things would get better for them.

answers.answer: I sincerely apologise for the mistake.
I sincere apologise for the mistake.
I apologise sincerely for the mistake.
I sincerely apologise about for the mistake.

sections.question: suddenly
sections.summary: Happening very quickly and unexpectedly; without any warning or preparation.

senses.definition: happening very quickly and unexpectedly; without any warning or advance notice
examples: She suddenly remembered where she had put her keys.

answers.answer: Suddenly, the lights went out.
The lights suddenly went out.
The lights went out sudden.
Suddenly, the lights went out at.

sections.question: surely
sections.summary: Used to express certainty or strong belief; without any doubt; definitely.

senses.definition: used to express strong belief or certainty about something; without doubt; also used to show surprise that something is not the case
examples: Surely there must be a better way to solve this problem.

answers.answer: Surely you can see the problem.
Surely you can to see the problem.
You can surely see the problem.
Surely, you can see about the problem.

sections.question: totally
sections.summary: Completely and in every way; used to give emphasis and mean to the fullest extent.

senses.definition: completely and in every way; used to give strong emphasis; to the fullest possible extent
examples: The two approaches are totally different from each other.

answers.answer: I totally forgot the appointment.
I total forgot the appointment.
I forgot totally the appointment.
I totally forgot about to the appointment.

sections.question: truly
sections.summary: In a genuine and sincere way; really and completely; used for emphasis.

senses.definition: in a genuine and sincere way; really and completely; used to emphasise that something is the case
examples: This is a truly remarkable achievement for the whole team.

answers.answer: I truly believe you can pass.
I true believe you can pass.
I believe truly you can pass.
I truly believe in you can pass.

sections.question: unexpectedly
sections.summary: In a way that was not predicted or anticipated; as a surprise.

senses.definition: in a way that was not predicted, planned, or anticipated; causing surprise because it was not foreseen
examples: The meeting ended unexpectedly when the power went out.

answers.answer: He arrived unexpectedly early.
He arrived unexpected early.
Unexpectedly he arrived early.
He arrived unexpectedly at early.

sections.question: utterly
sections.summary: Completely and absolutely; to the greatest possible degree; used for strong emphasis.

senses.definition: completely and absolutely; used to give very strong emphasis, often with negative adjectives or situations
examples: The whole situation was utterly confusing from start to finish.

answers.answer: I was utterly exhausted after the trip.
I was utter exhausted after the trip.
I utterly was exhausted after the trip.
I was utterly exhausted from to the trip.
